name: Apply ESOI to a Project
description: ESOI is a way to turn what someone means into a structure that keeps serving that meaning while both change. People and agents learn it and find their way around it; a project's records and code stay true and lean; evidence decides which way of doing each job is best; and that choice reaches the programs that run, without anyone rewriting them. A project can apply it with documents alone or add the tools, which check the records and move each selection to the measured winner.
purpose: Turn a project's intent into specifications that are checked, measured and selected by metric, so the structure keeps evolving with the intent.
approach: Start from plain documents and templates that anyone can fill in by hand (Understanding), then add checks (Structure), measurement and selection (Optimization) and the carrying of the choice into running programs (Runtime), so the records stay true to the intent.
out_of_scope: Deciding what a project is for: that is the project's own top intent.
milestones: 1. Adoption effort: one recorded newcomer trial applying ESOI from the documents only, and one with the tools.
knowledge: The author's skill: its definitions, the intent specification, the five specification templates and the principles; the adopters' experience.
measures_of_success: A newcomer applies ESOI from the documents alone with few questions, and a project's records pass the structure check. Standing conditions: A person or an agent can specify an intent, compare the alternatives of each solution by metric and let the best one be used, with every part reachable from the specifications.
parameters: The project's own top intent, and which implementations of the building blocks to use.
inputs: A project's intent, in its owner's words.
outputs: Specifications for the project (an intent folder with its five record types), checks and metric results.
effects: None beyond the files the project keeps.
usage_notes: Start from the documents and templates; add the Python tools where checks, measurement and selection should run by themselves.

name: Understanding
description: This is where ESOI meets people and agents. It holds the explanation and templates someone needs to start by hand, the order to work in, the published skill, the standing instructions that make an agent act by the principles, and the pages and searches that put the right records in front of a reader. It improves when the author refines what ESOI says or when readers need something different, even if no code changes.
purpose: Bring ESOI to the people and agents who apply it, in the author's own words, and let each of them find, read and steer the part of a structure in front of them.
approach: Compose the standard, the standing instructions for agents, the readable pages, the review tracker, the search and the local index, each measured and replaceable on its own. It stands apart from its siblings because its scores (adoption effort, steps followed, behaviour adherence, judge agreement, glanceability, review coverage, search correctness, index lookup) move when the author changes the skill or when readers need something different, even if no line of code changes; it is the only container whose metric is agreement with a person.
out_of_scope: Keeping records true to the code; measuring alternatives and choosing between them; serving an implementation inside a running program.
milestones: 1. The coherence of this container's intent: one paragraph and one diagram that explain its parts as the code builds them (metric-solution-coherence).
knowledge: The author's skill and its principles; the documentation standard that `esoi docs check` enforces.
measures_of_success: A newcomer applies ESOI from what Understanding gives alone, an agent acts by the principles, and a reader finds the part of a project that bears on their work. Standing conditions: each part reports on a project in one read-only call.
parameters: The project folder.
inputs: A project folder.
outputs: One read-only report from each part: what each says about the project.
effects: Reads the project's records and documents; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `esoi.run("esoi-understanding", ".")` returns the report of each part.

name: Structure
description: This is the project's own form: the linked records, the template they follow, the map from every file to its purpose, the rules that keep it all in shape, and the budget that keeps the structure from costing more than it returns. It changes when the project's records, template or code change.
purpose: Keep a project's records and code one true and lean structure that says why every part exists and improves itself where it falls short.
approach: Compose the registry of records, the map from files to solutions, the structural check and the budget that keeps the structure proportionate. It stands apart from its siblings because its scores (record completeness, navigable records, template agreement, trace completeness, violation detection, cost against catches) move when a project's records, its template or its code change: a new file, a drifted row, a refined field.
out_of_scope: Teaching ESOI and showing records to readers; measuring and selecting implementations; choosing at run time.
milestones: 1. The coherence of this container's intent: one paragraph and one diagram that explain its parts as the code builds them (metric-solution-coherence).
knowledge: The intent template in the author's skill; requirements traceability practice; architecture tests and linters.
measures_of_success: Every file reaches a solution, every record is complete and every link resolves both ways, and the structural check passes. Standing conditions: each part reports on a project in one read-only call.
parameters: The project folder.
inputs: A project folder.
outputs: One read-only report from each part: records counted, files unowned, findings by rule and the budget.
effects: Reads the project's records and code; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `esoi.run("esoi-structure", ".")` returns the report of each part and whether the coherence gate passes.

name: Optimization
description: This is how a project comes to run its best implementations on evidence rather than habit. It runs the shipped code on fixed cases, proves the cases can fail, decides when a run is worth its cost (checking first whether the result is still current and whether others have already measured it), calls winners only beyond the noise, switches the selection, and keeps a before-and-after record of each piece of work. It improves when new implementations, cases or results arrive.
purpose: Make each solution run the implementation the evidence shows is best, with evidence that is trustworthy, current and worth what it cost.
approach: Compose the harness that measures, the decision of when to measure, the leaderboard that judges, the promotion that switches and the record of each piece of work. It stands apart from its siblings because its scores (provenance completeness, case discrimination, ranking correctness, staleness precision, public evidence graded, promotion correctness, decisions backed by current results, metric record kept) move when evidence changes: a new arm, a new case set, a new public result. It is the Optimizes in ESOI's name. For ESOI the driver ML task accuracy is read as how accurately evidence is gathered and judged.
out_of_scope: Keeping records true; serving the selected implementation inside a program; teaching.
milestones: 1. The coherence of this container's intent: one paragraph and one diagram that explain its parts as the code builds them (metric-solution-coherence).
knowledge: Evaluation harnesses, ranking by probability, model registries and promotion gates; public benchmark practice.
measures_of_success: Each solution's selected implementation is the measured winner or a declared tie, on evidence that is current and traceable. Standing conditions: each part reports on a project in one read-only call.
parameters: The project folder.
inputs: A project folder.
outputs: One read-only report from each part: components measured, what a run costs, the standings, the proposals and the metric readings.
effects: Reads the project's records and results; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `esoi.run("esoi-optimization", ".")` returns the report of each part.

name: Runtime
description: This is ESOI inside programs that are running for someone. A program declares its alternatives where its code defines them; each call is served by the selected one; whole programs are assembled from named parts with their environment needs checked; and a system built on the library can show that it meets the library's standard and see how far behind it is.
purpose: Carry ESOI into other people's running programs, so a better measurement changes what runs without anyone editing a call site.
approach: Compose the selection of an implementation per call, the assembly of whole programs from named parts and the check of a consumer's system against the library. It stands apart from its siblings because its scores (resolution correctness, assembly cases, consumer soundness) move when the embedding programs, their environments or their pinned versions change, all outside this repository.
out_of_scope: Deciding which implementation is best; keeping the records; teaching.
milestones: 1. The coherence of this container's intent: one paragraph and one diagram that explain its parts as the code builds them (metric-solution-coherence).
knowledge: Ports and adapters; plugin registries; dependency injection containers; lazy loading of optional dependencies.
measures_of_success: Every switch of an implementation works from configuration alone, a program is assembled from names, and a consumer sees how far its pins trail. Standing conditions: each part reports in one read-only call.
parameters: A solution id to show the parts on.
inputs: A solution id.
outputs: One read-only report from each part: the choice for the solution, the names it assembles and the ids a consumer knows.
effects: Imports the chosen implementation lazily; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `esoi.run("esoi-runtime", "structure-check")` returns the report of each part.

name: Keep a Metric Record
description: Lets a program keep a piece of work's metric value before and after the change itself, so the record never rests on the worker's closing words.
purpose: Keep the relevant metric's value before and after each piece of work, so the change can be judged later.
approach: Find the solution a request serves and its next milestone, read the metric with a bounded meter before and after the work, and keep the readings as rows in a ledger that the worker's own claims can sit beside.
out_of_scope: Choosing the metric; finding the slice of the specification; calling a model.
milestones: 1. Metric record correctness: every offline case of the live record implementation passes (slice, milestone, reading, result, reconcile, iteration and arm cases).
knowledge: ESOI's rule for work is the relevant metric result before and after the change; a worker's closing words are only a claim, so a program takes the reading; a recorded row says nothing about a tree that has changed since, so a reading after the work is taken from the tree as it is now.
measures_of_success: Every offline case of the live record implementation passes. Standing conditions: A reading never holds the work back past its budget; a reading with no number writes no row; the slice lookup, the meters and the ledger never raise into the work they record and never call a model.
parameters: MetricIteration: ledger, run_id, source, meters, measures, task_id, request, working_dir, status, budget_seconds (15 by default), closing, statuses. meters_from_names(names, environ) builds the meters (recorded_row, offline_arm).
inputs: A ledger directory and a run id, the request text and working folder, a slice source and the meters; the repository's records and results log are read through them.
outputs: From begin, the NEXT PRIORITY block for the brief; from finish, the reconciled MetricResult rows (solution_id, metric_id, name, milestone, before, after, delta, source, reason, disagrees) and whether the work did anything for them to describe.
effects: Writes one JSON-lines file per run in the ledger directory. The offline_arm meter runs the metric's esoi run command with zero model calls and a time limit, and only for an arm that cannot spend money.
usage_notes: Create one MetricIteration per piece of work, call begin before the first attempt and finish after the last. With no source it adds nothing, a source alone gives the slice for the brief, and a source with meters also reads the metric before and after; an ambiguous request gets no slice and a metric no meter can read gets no reading. See docs/how-to/measure-before-and-after.md.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Implementation Leaderboard
description: Turns recorded results into an honest verdict on which implementation is best, and says so plainly when the result is a tie or the evidence is not comparable.
purpose: Decide from recorded results which implementation is best, or whether they tie.
approach: Compare the recorded scores of the implementations on the same cases and call a winner only when the gap is beyond the noise.
out_of_scope: Running; switching the selection.
milestones: 1. Ranking correctness: the verdict matches the known right verdict on every pinned result set, ties and different case sets included. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Statistical noise in small judged samples; cost and token accounting; Pareto comparison of quality and cost.
measures_of_success: Its verdicts match known rankings on pinned cases and never call a tie a win. Standing conditions: A win is called only outside the noise margin; ties, losses and unmeasured arms are labelled as such; comparison-only arms are never rivals.
parameters: Noise margin and spend tolerance per component.
inputs: The results log.
outputs: A verdict per solution and a ranked board.
effects: None.
usage_notes: The check requires the selected implementation to be the winner or a declared tie with a reason.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Measurement Harness
description: Makes every result trustworthy by running the code that ships against the solution's cases and recording where the result came from, so anyone can rerun it.
purpose: Run each implementation against its solution's cases through the shipped code, and record each result with its provenance.
approach: Drive the shipped implementation over fixed cases and record each score with its commit, case hash, cost and tokens under a call budget.
out_of_scope: Ranking; deciding whether a run is worth it.
milestones: 1. Provenance completeness: every latest result has a clean commit, a case hash, cost and tokens, run through shipped code, and all provenance cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Evaluation practice for language models (held-out cases, staged sample sizes, judged rubrics); experiment tracking; the eval ladder of three, ten and thirty cases.
measures_of_success: Any result can be rerun from its record, and no result was produced by code other than what ships. Standing conditions: Every eval solution has cases, a scorer and implementations that drive shipped code; every recorded result carries its commit, case hash, cost and tokens; a call budget stops a run.
parameters: Solution, implementation, case subset, call budget.
inputs: Case files, the implementation, any live services the cases need.
outputs: A results row per run.
effects: Model spend on live runs; refuses to run against production.
usage_notes: Start live runs small and stop at the budget; re-record on committed code after any change to measured code or cases.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Promote the Winner
description: Moves a project to its best implementation on evidence, with the proof attached, and stops short of the switch when a person must approve it.
purpose: Switch the selection to the rival that clearly wins on the solution's own metric, with the evidence recorded, or propose it when a person must approve.
approach: Switch the selection only on current, comparable, verified results beyond the noise, and otherwise propose the exact change.
out_of_scope: Deciding what is best; promoting on stale or incomparable results.
milestones: 1. Promotion correctness: a winner is promoted only on current, comparable, verified results beyond the noise, and the exact proposal is printed otherwise. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Model registry promotion gates; the leaderboard's same-cases comparison and noise margins.
measures_of_success: A switch happens only on current, comparable, verified results beyond the noise and only where the solution allows it; otherwise the exact proposal is printed. Standing conditions: A clear winner becomes the selected implementation without hand editing, and every switch carries its evidence.
parameters: A solution id (optional) and a dry run.
inputs: The results log, the records, and the `promotion` cell of each solution.
outputs: Edits to selected, selected_by and the metric's command, or a printed proposal.
effects: Rewrites the solution and metric rows and rebuilds the review tracker.
usage_notes: Put `automatic` in a solution's `promotion` cell where its policy lets the metric decide; leave it empty to review each proposal.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: When Metrics Are Run
description: Ensures decisions rest on current evidence and that spending on measurement is approved and proportionate, by settling in advance when each metric runs.
purpose: Decide when each metric is run, in what stages, with what limit, who approves the spend, and when its result stops counting.
approach: Set for each metric its stages, a call budget, who approves the spend and what makes its result stale, and run it when what it would teach is worth its cost; a stale result informs and orders no run.
out_of_scope: How a metric is implemented; which alternative wins.
milestones: 1. Decisions backed by current results: every staleness case passes, so a stale or missing result is reported and a current one is not. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Evaluation practice for models (staged and stratified samples, call budgets, noise); continuous integration practice; the cost of re-running against the cost of deciding wrongly.
measures_of_success: Decisions are backed by current results, spend is approved and proportionate, and stale results are found at the change rather than at a release. Standing conditions: Offline metrics run on every change; paid metrics run only when a decision depends on them, in staged samples; every recorded result can be told current from stale.
parameters: Trigger: every change for the offline metrics, in the test suite and in continuous integration; a paid metric only when a decision depends on it, in staged samples inside a call budget and with Joshua's approval.
inputs: The committed code, the case files and the results log.
outputs: A row per run in the results log with the commit and the hash of the cases; the strict check's verdict.
effects: Offline metrics call no paid service and no network; a paid metric calls a model only when it is run on a decision. Re-recording changes only the results log.
usage_notes: After committing measured code or cases, `esoi run --stale --plan` shows which results no longer describe the code; re-record with `esoi run --stale --for-decision` when a decision or release depends on them, then commit the results log. An arm that calls a model needs a cost estimate, a staged sample and Joshua's approval first.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Assemble Parts by Name
description: Lets one solution's implementation need another by name instead of by import, so configuration can swap a part and a missing or circular need fails when the program starts.
purpose: Build a program's parts from validated names in dependency order, so each part depends on a solution and never on one implementation, and check what each needs from its environment.
approach: Validate each name against the solution's listed implementations, load only modules that a record names, resolve each part through the cascade of explicit name, selections, environment, lock and package default, and build the parts in dependency order.
out_of_scope: Choosing each part (it asks Implementation Selection); importing a module no record names.
milestones: 1. Assembly correctness: every offline case of the live assembler passes, hostile names, cycles, unmet needs and concurrent assembles included.
knowledge: Implementations depend on solutions, never on other implementations; a name is data, while an import path read from a file runs code nobody reviewed; a cycle or an unmet need is cheaper to find at startup than on the first call that reaches it. See docs/explanation/cross-dependency-by-name.md.
measures_of_success: Every offline case of the live assembler passes. Standing conditions: A hostile name, snapshot or parent configuration runs nothing; a cycle or a need nothing meets fails at startup naming the chain; the assembled system is frozen once built.
parameters: Assembler: scope, package_dir, modules, records, parent. AssemblyConfig: solutions, selections, options, selection_environ, consumer_environ, lock, circumstances. assemble(config, provided=...).
inputs: The package's scope and folder, the solutions to build, the consumer's selections, options and ready objects, and the records or packaged snapshot that name the implementations and each solution's default.
outputs: A frozen Assembly: the built part of each solution in dependency order, with the choice and reason line of each (choice, implementation, reasons); explain lists every layer of one solution.
effects: Imports a module only when a record of the package names it and its file lies inside the package folder; leaves sys.path unchanged; reads no environment beyond the mapping it is given; raises at startup on a cycle or an unmet need.
usage_notes: Declare each solution once as a Protocol with @solution, type a constructor parameter with it to need it, build one Assembler(scope, folder, modules=...) in the package and call assemble(AssemblyConfig(...)) at startup. See docs/how-to/assemble-by-name.md.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Consumer Check
description: Lets a system built on the library prove it uses the library's solutions correctly, without copying the library's checks or exposing its own data.
purpose: Let a system built on the library show which library solution each part serves, score its parts on the library's cases by building on the library's metric, and see how far its pins trail.
approach: Map each integration point to a library solution, score the consumer's stores with the library's cases, and report how far its pinned version trails.
out_of_scope: Copying the library's checks; putting the consumer's private data in the library; switching the consumer's selection for it.
milestones: 1. Consumer soundness: no unmapped integration point, no consumer store unscored by the library's cases, and the pin lag visible, and all consumer cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Consumer-driven contract testing; the library's own structure check and cases.
measures_of_success: The consumer passes with nothing unmapped, unscored or unexplained. Standing conditions: Every integration point maps to a library solution; every consumer store is scored by the library's cases; the pin's lag is visible.
parameters: The consumer's registry, root, requirements, solutions and results files; whether lag fails.
inputs: The consumer repository.
outputs: Violations and notes.
effects: None.
usage_notes: Run in the consumer's tests; bump the pin after the library's changes land.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Implementation Selection
description: Lets a project and a running program switch between alternatives by changing data, and fails loudly on a mistyped name instead of quietly running something else. A call is served by the implementation that a per-call name, an override, the environment, the lock or the recorded default chooses.
purpose: Choose which implementation serves a call, by a per-call name, an override, the environment, the lock or the recorded default, and refuse an unknown name by listing the valid choices.
approach: Resolve the implementation from a per-call name, an override, an environment setting, the lock or the recorded default, through declarations in code with one cascade or through a selection table, and refuse an unknown name by listing the valid choices.
out_of_scope: Deciding which is best; branching at every call site.
milestones: 1. Resolution correctness: a recorded run of the entry-point rival and of the chosen implementation on the selection cases. 2. Runtime selection: the selector resolves every selection case as specified: name, override, environment and table default.
knowledge: Ports and adapters; plugin registries; lazy loading of optional dependencies; how libraries let an embedding program declare and select alternatives.
measures_of_success: Every switch works from configuration alone and no typo falls back silently. Standing conditions: Switching is a data change; an unknown name fails with the choices; every listed implementation loads; a program that embeds the package carries no second copy of the default.
parameters: Solution id, implementation name per call, a context block, an environment variable, a deployment table, configuration overrides.
inputs: The implementations declared in code, the records' selected cell, an optional selection table of module:Attribute targets.
outputs: The chosen implementation's class and its configuration type.
effects: Imports the chosen implementation lazily.
usage_notes: Every swappable solution has declared implementations and a selected cell whose value equals the measured winner or a declared tie. The records' selected cell is the project default; let the metric decide it and leave it out of any selection table.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Intent Registry
description: Keeps a project's whole intent as one set of linked records that a person and a program read the same way, so the reasons behind the code never live only in someone's head.
purpose: Record every problem, solution, implementation, ideal and metric of a project as linked records that people and checks both read.
approach: Store each intent item as one record with fixed fields and links that resolve in both directions.
out_of_scope: Measured results; pages for readers.
milestones: 1. Record completeness: every record has every template field filled and every link resolving both ways, and all record cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26] 2. Navigable records: for each solution, its spec and its code are in the same folder or one link apart, the spec is within three clicks of the top README, no record is kept twice, and each folder that holds an implementation has a README.
knowledge: The intent template in the evolvable-structure skill; Joshua's Project Documentation board (solution definitions apart from implementations); requirements traceability practice.
measures_of_success: A reader can follow any file to its problem and ideal, and every record is complete. Standing conditions: Every intent item is one record with every template field filled; every link resolves both ways; every file reaches a solution through the ownership map.
parameters: The template's fields per type.
inputs: Hand-edited records of each type, the ownership map.
outputs: A linked intent network that the check, the tracker and the selection read.
effects: None.
usage_notes: Add or edit a record before building a new capability; the check names anything missing.
verdict_detail: beside_code is better than esoi_folder (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=2.38e-07, 23 of 50 cases disagree)

name: Library Adoption
description: An application that needs a job a library already defines refers to the library's solution instead of copying its records, so each job is defined once. The application's records hold three kinds of solution: adopted ones that are only a reference, specialized ones that add what needs the application's data, and its own, which carry its own metrics, customization and code.
purpose: Let a repository refer to a solution that another library's records define, and tell the adopted, the specialized and its own solutions apart, so no job is described twice.
approach: A row of solutions.csv names the library solution it adopts or specializes as @library/solution_id; the library's repository is named in the configuration; the checks resolve each reference and inform of restated jobs; the generated page links an adopted solution to the library's page.
out_of_scope: Reading and writing the records themselves (Intent Registry); running the rules (Structure Check); drawing the pages (Readable Records); reusing the library's measured results, which is a metric building on its foundation (Consumer Check); deciding that two jobs are the same, which a person does.
milestones: 1. Resolution: every reference in the fixtures resolves or is reported with its next action, and all adoption cases pass.
knowledge: The records standard and its cross-project reference form @project/solution; the practice of depending on a published interface instead of vendoring its source.
measures_of_success: A reader can name, for each solution of an adopting repository, whether it is adopted, specialized or its own, and no adopted solution restates the library. Standing conditions: every reference resolves to a solution of a readable library.
parameters: The library names and repositories under [adopts] in the configuration.
inputs: The solutions.csv rows with an adopts or specializes cell, and the library's records.
outputs: The references that do not resolve, and for each adopted solution the library's own description and page.
effects: None beyond reading the library's records.
usage_notes: `esoi.run("library-adoption", ".")` lists the references that do not resolve; the steps are in docs/how-to/adopt-a-solution-from-a-library.md.

name: Ownership Map
description: Shows that every file exists for a reason by tracing it to the problem and ideal it serves, so code that serves nothing is found and removed.
purpose: Assign every file to exactly one component and every component to the solutions it serves, so code with no purpose cannot hide.
approach: Give each file one owner and trace that owner through its solutions to a problem and an ideal.
out_of_scope: Describing what code does; deciding whether a part is worth its cost.
milestones: 1. Trace completeness: every file reaches a problem and an ideal through a component and a solution, and all ownership cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Layered and hexagonal architecture; code owners practice; the repository's split rule.
measures_of_success: Code that serves no solution is found and removed. Standing conditions: No file unowned, no component serving nothing, no module past the size ceiling, imports pointing inward.
parameters: Layer order, size ceiling.
inputs: The file tree and the component records.
outputs: File-to-solution links and the generated component index.
effects: None.
usage_notes: A new file joins a component in the same change; a file that fits no solution is a sign the code should go.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Structure Budget
description: Keeps the structure from turning into overhead: a rule, record or sub-intent is admitted only with what it prevents, and what stops paying is pruned, by weighing what the structure costs each change against what it catches.
purpose: Keep the structure's own cost in view: admit a rule, record or sub-intent only with what it prevents, and prune what stops paying.
approach: Admit a rule only with the mistake it prevents and evidence that it still catches something; weigh the effort the structure adds to each change against the real mistakes it catches, and remove what catches nothing.
out_of_scope: Removing what still catches real mistakes; running the rules.
milestones: 1. Structure cost against catches: the time the check adds and the real violations it caught, recorded over a month.
knowledge: Principle 12 (minimalism) and the skill's difficulties; developer-experience research; the repository's numbered rules.
measures_of_success: Small changes stay small and every rule has caught something real. Standing conditions: The effort the structure adds to a change is known; each rule has the mistake that justifies it; rules, records and checks that catch nothing are removed.
parameters: None yet.
inputs: The check's history, time per check, files touched per change.
outputs: A periodic report of cost against catches.
effects: Proposes removals.
usage_notes: Not built yet beyond the written weighing rule and the ratchet that shows how waivers, enabled rules and floors moved since a base commit.

name: Structure Check
description: Runs every structural rule on each change quickly enough that nobody skips it, reports each finding by rule and path with its next action, and keeps rule exceptions honest by reporting those that no longer apply. The rules are numbered modules written to one interface, each with the one-line statement of what it checks.
purpose: Run every structural rule on each change and report each finding by rule and path with its next action, quickly enough that nobody skips it.
approach: Run every enabled rule against the tree, report findings by rule id and path with the next action, and flag any accepted exception that no longer applies. A rule is a numbered module written to one interface, shipped with the library and extended by plugins.
out_of_scope: Deciding whether a rule earns its place; judging quality beyond the rules.
milestones: 1. Violation detection: every injected violation is reported by the right rule and path. [met: 2026-10-26] 2. Check dependability: a clean tree is never flagged and an exception that no longer applies is always reported, and all mutation cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Architecture tests and linters (import-linter, ArchUnit); plugin systems; the repository's numbered rules (esoi rules); the leaderboard (reused, not copied).
measures_of_success: Every injected violation is reported by the right rule and path, a clean tree is never flagged, an exception that no longer applies is reported, and the run is fast enough that nobody skips it. Standing conditions: Any rule written to the rule interface runs and reports by rule and path; a repository can disable a rule or add its own; each rule catches a mistake that has happened.
parameters: Strict mode; the rule ids to disable; the plugins to load; per-rule settings such as the module size ceiling and the layers.
inputs: The repository, the registry, the results log, the waivers, the configuration.
outputs: A list of violations, each led by its rule id, and an exit code.
effects: Blocks a commit or a test run that breaks a rule.
usage_notes: Keep the runner free of any one rule: a new rule is a rule group written to the interface, never an edit to the runner. Add a rule when a mistake has happened twice; whether a rule stays is the business of the structure budget.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Structure Quality
description: Scores how well a project's code and records divide the work, so scoping and modularity are judged by a number and its worst offenders instead of by whoever reads the whole tree: one job per solution, parts small and simple enough to read, connections only through declared entry points or the project's shared kernel, no copied code, a public surface that is used, and behavior held by a contract that runs every arm.
purpose: Measure how well a project divides its work into solutions and parts, as one balanced number with the worst offenders named, before and after code exists.
approach: Read the code and records without running them, score seven dimensions (scope, size, coupling, reuse, flow fidelity, public surface, behavior preserved) against budgets fixed beforehand, graded by how far a part goes over its budget where size is concerned, with the project's shared kernel told apart from another solution's internals, weight them into one number no single dimension can win, and mine the git history for files that change together across solutions as a second, more faithful stage of the same number.
out_of_scope: Running the structural rules on each change; deciding whether a rule earns its place; the correctness of what any one part produces; deciding that a solution's purpose is worth having.
milestones: 1. Stage one scores every dimension offline on small cases and on whole repositories. [met: 2026-11-05] 2. Stage two reads co-change from git history. [met: 2026-11-05] 3. The expert review of scoping is specified and costed, not run. [met: 2026-11-05] 4. A consumer states its own budgets and cases on top of this metric and keeps no copy of the scorer.
knowledge: Ousterhout on deep modules and pass-through methods; Parnas on information hiding; Martin's instability metric and the stable dependencies, acyclic dependencies, common reuse and interface segregation principles (the shared kernel and the fat interface); McCabe's cyclomatic complexity; PEP 8 on a package's __init__ as its interface; clone detection by token windows; logical coupling from co-change in version history (Gall, Zimmermann); esoi's own S48, S49 and coherence evidence.
measures_of_success: The balanced number agrees with labelled structural incidents: a clean exemplar is sound, each incident flags the dimension it damages, and the project cut into tiny files scores below the balanced real structure that a size-only scorer prefers. Standing conditions: weights and budgets are fixed before any alternative is scored; a dimension that cannot be measured is reported as not measured, never as perfect; findings inform and never fail a check.
parameters: The project path, the stage (1 static, 2 adds history), and the budgets a consumer may tighten (function and module lines, complexity per function, files per folder, solutions per intent, depth, Protocols per unit, the clone window, the importers and instability of a shared kernel, the consumers a library must not name).
inputs: The project's Python files, its records beside the code, its test files, the coherence gate's report where records exist, and at stage two its git history.
outputs: One balanced number from 0 to 1, each dimension's score, the dimensions flagged and each one's worst offenders
effects: None: it reads and reports. Structure Check's advisory rules print its findings.
usage_notes: Run `esoi structure-quality [--stage 1|2] [path]`. Weights are fixed in `balance.py`; a consumer tightens budgets and adds cases, never a copy of the scorer (`[builds_on]`). A single-factor score such as file size alone is the bound the balanced number must beat, since shrinking files wins it.
verdict_detail: balanced_static is better than file_size_only (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1.41e-07, 44 of 49 cases disagree)

name: ESOI Applied to AI Behaviour
description: Makes an AI agent apply the principles in its own work, and shows by measurement which way of giving it the principles works.
purpose: Make an AI agent act by the evolvable-structure principles when designing, building, writing and advising.
approach: Give the agent the principles in a chosen form and measure, case by case, whether its replies act on them compared with the same agent without them.
out_of_scope: Teaching people; finding which records or standards bear on a task; general agent ability.
milestones: 1. Behaviour adherence: a recorded run of each arm that calls a model, on the staged sample.
knowledge: The author's skill and its principles, especially principle 4 (humans need only review metrics, not implementations, though they can still add value to implementations) and principle 7 (perspectives are implementations); evaluation practice for language models (cases with an expected behaviour and a failure mode, staged samples, a no-instructions baseline); practice for loading skills and standing instructions.
measures_of_success: The share of cases where the agent's reply acts by the principle, per principle, compared with the same agent without the instructions, with restraint and kept-qualifier cases counted as often as build cases. Standing conditions: Cases cover every principle, including cases where the right behaviour is to hold back or to keep a qualifier; each way of giving the agent the principles is measured on the same cases; the instructions in use are the measured winner or a declared tie; the closing summary of every use says how the principles were applied.
parameters: The model, the way the principles are given (standing instructions, on request, none), the case subset and a call budget.
inputs: A task prompt an agent might be sent.
outputs: The agent's reply and, for a judged run, a verdict with a reason.
effects: A live measurement calls a model and costs money; nothing else.
usage_notes: Run the offline checks after changing the cases or esoi.understanding.esoi_for_ai.behaviour (the reference_good and reference_bad arms need no model); run an arm that calls a model only when a decision depends on it and the spend is approved (esoi/metric-run-policy.md). A person who corrects an agent's behaviour adds or edits a case, not only the instructions, so the correction is measured from then on.
verdict_detail: the selected implementation has no recorded row; no arm has a result

name: Local ESOI Index
description: Answers where to look for a project from the person's own index, so it works for projects no guidance ever named.
purpose: Find which projects ESOI is applied to, how they relate and where to look first in each.
approach: Look the project up in the person's own index of pointers and relations, and answer none for a path outside every project.
out_of_scope: Anything about a project beyond a pointer and its relations; which records inside a project bear on a request.
milestones: 1. Local index lookup: the live lookup passes every lookup case, including projects the guidance never named and paths outside every project. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: How the folder for a tool's user settings works in other tools; the principle of finding and reusing structure instead of rebuilding it.
measures_of_success: The lookup cases pass for projects the guidance never named, and a lookup that routes from frozen rows or from a project's records alone fails them. Standing conditions: A question about where to look is answered for any listed project, including one added later, and for a path outside every project the answer is none.
parameters: Where the index folder is (an environment variable, else a folder in the user's home).
inputs: A path, a project id or a request to list.
outputs: The project containing the path with its first file to read and its specifications, the ids related in a given way, or the listed ids.
effects: Writes only the index folder; makes no network call.
usage_notes: The skill's index says to read the person's local index first; the commands `esoi projects init`, `add`, `check`, `index` and `where` keep it.
verdict_detail: live_index is better than records_only (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0312, 7 of 10 cases disagree); live_index leads skill_rows (skill_rows 0.6 against live_index 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.125, 4 of 10 cases disagree)

name: Readable Records
description: Gives every intent folder a page that cannot disagree with its records, because the page is made from them.
purpose: Give every intent folder a page, made from its records, that says at a glance what the intent is and how its parts fit.
approach: Generate the page from the records and report any page that no longer matches them.
out_of_scope: Holding records; carrying a reviewer's edits back.
milestones: 1. README fidelity: the generated page equals what the records say, and a page that no longer matches is reported. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Generated indexes of components; README conventions; the intent specification in the author's skill.
measures_of_success: The page states the intent and lists every record by id, and the check reports a page that no longer matches its records. Standing conditions: Opening a folder tells a reader what the intent is for, and the page cannot disagree with the records.
parameters: None.
inputs: The records of one intent.
outputs: A README.md in the intent's folder.
effects: Writes README.md in each intent folder when the docs are regenerated.
usage_notes: Run `esoi check --write-docs` after editing records; edit the CSV files, never the page.
verdict_detail: at_a_glance leads full_page (full_page 0 against at_a_glance 0.5; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=1, 2 of 4 cases disagree); at_a_glance leads links_page (links_page 0 against at_a_glance 0.5; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=1, 2 of 4 cases disagree)

name: Review Tracker
description: Lets a reviewer see the whole intent network and its latest results in one place and make decisions there, without learning the repository layout.
purpose: Put the whole intent network and its current results in front of a reviewer, and carry their edits back to the records.
approach: Build one review view from the records and results, and return the reviewer's edits to the records so that rebuilds keep them.
out_of_scope: Holding truth beyond the review columns; calling verdicts.
milestones: 1. Review coverage: every record and verdict is present in the sheet and every reviewer edit survives a rebuild and reaches the repository, and all tracker cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Spreadsheets as the team's review medium; two-way sync keyed by record id.
measures_of_success: Joshua can make and record every review decision from the sheet. Standing conditions: Every record and its latest verdict appears in one sheet; reviewer edits survive rebuilds and flow back to the repository.
parameters: Which tabs, which columns a reviewer may edit.
inputs: The registry and the results log.
outputs: Generated tracker tables and the synced sheet.
effects: Writes the sheet.
usage_notes: Rebuild after any registry or result change; the check fails when the tracker is stale.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Spec Search
description: Gives any system one search over a repository's records, standards and its own items, cheapest first, with the semantic search and the judge supplied by the caller, so no model or embedding lives in the library. Its first stage is the model-free lexical index, which stays available alone as the weighted-terms arms.
purpose: Find the records, standards and product items that a request concerns, cheapest first, each with the records it links to.
approach: Score the records lexically with the index's own formula, fuse that ranking with an optional semantic search the caller supplies, let only confident results through a gate with named thresholds, and let a judge the caller supplies choose at most once, keeping the candidates when it fails.
out_of_scope: Embeddings, vector stores, prompts and model calls, which the caller supplies; judging what the work is worth.
milestones: 1. Spec search correctness: the offline cases over the live records pass, 6 of 6. 2. Each adopter's search is a thin binding over this module and measures its own vector search and judge on its own records. 3. Spec index recall: for labelled requests the expected records appear in the top results, and the first stage's scan of all records stays a small fraction of the full records.
knowledge: Reciprocal rank fusion; field-weighted TF-IDF as the Quest AI runner uses for context cards; progressive disclosure; confidence-gated model use; the intent records' own link columns.
measures_of_success: Offline cases over the live records pass for the selected arm and the lexical baseline is no better; adopters hold no copy of the stages.
parameters: strategy (gated, judge-all, lexical); k_lexical and k_vector; max_ranked; expand; ranked_kinds and link_kinds; tags and tag_mode; the Gate thresholds; batch_size; unjudged_top; for the index stage k, how many records to return, and tier, how much of one record to show.
inputs: A request text, a list of views (from the index or from the caller's items), and optionally vector_search(text, k) and judge(task, lines, limit).
outputs: A Selection: ranked items best first with their linked items, the candidates, which search proposed each, the number of judge calls, the route and the no-solution cue.
effects: None of its own: it calls only the functions the caller injects. A failing vector search or judge leaves the lexical or fused answer.
usage_notes: Build views with views_from_index and views_from_items, call search(task, views, judge=..., vector_search=...). `esoi spec find TEXT` narrows by the index alone and `esoi spec show ID --tier N` reads one record. See docs/how-to/search-specs-and-items.md.
verdict_detail: lexical_only is exactly equal to gated on the metric (lexical_only 1 against gated 1), so gated stays

name: The Standard
description: Gives a newcomer explanation, fill-in templates and one document that shows end to end how a solution is shaped and how to adopt that shape in another repository, so a person or an agent can apply ESOI by hand before any tool is installed. Its metric is the one where the best is a newcomer reaching a passing application by reading alone.
purpose: Teach anyone, person or AI, how a solution is shaped and how a project adopts it, with explanation and fill-in templates that need no code.
approach: Lay out the shape of a solution and the steps to adopt it in documents that can be followed alone: explain each idea in plain words and provide templates that can be filled in without code.
out_of_scope: What the automated checks already enforce; making an agent act by the principles.
milestones: 1. Adoption effort: one recorded newcomer trial of following only the standard in a fresh repository. 2. Newcomer effort: one recorded run of a newcomer following the guides in a fresh repository.
knowledge: The adopting repositories as worked examples; the evolvable-structure skill: its definitions, principles and intent template, quoted.
measures_of_success: Someone following it alone reaches a passing check. Standing conditions: One document gives the shape of a solution end to end and the steps to adopt it elsewhere; A newcomer can write an overall network and a first solution from the templates alone.
parameters: None.
inputs: The registry's rules and examples; the skill's SKILL.md.
outputs: The standard document, explanations, guides and generated templates.
effects: None.
usage_notes: Read the explanation first, then copy a template; update the standard in the same change as any rule.

name: Discriminating Cases
description: Shows that a solution's cases can actually fail, which is the only evidence a measure has when the solution has no rival to compare against.
purpose: Prove that a solution's cases can tell a sound implementation from a naive one, even when only one implementation exists.
approach: Write deliberately naive implementations and show that each one fails the cases.
out_of_scope: Inventing rivals that exist only to lose a comparison.
milestones: 1. Case discrimination: a recorded run of the share of solutions whose naive baselines all fail their cases.
knowledge: Mutation testing; the gap between a passing test and a meaningful one.
measures_of_success: No case set passes everything that is put in front of it. Standing conditions: Every invariant solution has at least one naive baseline that fails its cases.
parameters: None.
inputs: A solution's cases and its naive baselines.
outputs: A pass or fail per baseline.
effects: None.
usage_notes: Write the naive version a first draft would produce, not a deliberately silly one.

name: Know What a Result Measures
description: Decides which changed files make a recorded result stale, by what the result's arm measures instead of by the whole repository.
purpose: Tell, for one recorded result, whether the code, cases or circumstances it measures changed since its commit, and say which changed file and which component's ownership explains the answer.
approach: Compare the files changed since a result's commit with the files that result's arm measures (its own code, never test files, shared fixtures or another arm's code), and name the changed file and the component that owns it; a result whose measured files cannot be told apart counts every measured file, so it is never silently fresh.
out_of_scope: Deciding when a stale result is run again, and how the metric itself is implemented.
milestones: 1. Staleness precision: no staleness case keeps a result whose measured code changed, and the selected rule re-runs for nothing in fewer cases than the whole-repository rule.
knowledge: Static import analysis; the ownership map of this repository; the cost of a needless re-run against the cost of trusting a result whose code changed.
measures_of_success: No result is kept whose measured code changed, and a commit to one component leaves the results of the others current. Standing conditions: an arm without an ownership entry keeps the whole-repository rule; a changed file informs and never blocks a commit.
parameters: staleness_rule in esoi.toml: repo_wide, component_paths or import_closure; otherwise the arm the records select for this solution.
inputs: The results row (its commit), the files changed since that commit in the working tree, the ownership map (components.csv), the implementation records and the arm's source.
outputs: Stale or current for the row, the reason naming the changed file and its owner, and the files that were ignored with their owners.
effects: Reads git and the source files; runs nothing from the measured code and calls no model.
usage_notes: `esoi stale --explain COMPONENT` lists, per arm, the changed files that count and the ones ignored; `esoi stale --count` counts the rows each rule calls stale now.
verdict_detail: import_closure is better than component_paths (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.000488, 12 of 55 cases disagree); import_closure is better than repo_wide (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=2.33e-10, 34 of 55 cases disagree)

name: Grade Public Evidence
description: Judges what others measured by a visible table of weights, with no model call, so an outside result informs what to measure without replacing the repository's own results.
purpose: Grade what others have measured about a candidate, so a measurement that costs money is made only when outside evidence cannot settle the question.
approach: Group each reported number by measure and comparator, score its source, independence, method, sample, benchmark status, age and confounds, cap the letter by what the sources are, and raise or lower it when sources agree or contradict.
out_of_scope: Searching the literature for more evidence, merging different measures or comparators, converting units outside the table, and replacing the repository's own results.
milestones: 1. Evidence grading correctness: every offline case of the graded implementation passes (grades and rankings).
knowledge: One number is one number; a vendor measured its own product; a benchmark everyone tops separates nothing; a harness difference looks like a model difference. Each weight of the grading table carries its reason (esoi evidence table).
measures_of_success: Every offline case of the graded implementation passes. Standing conditions: Every grade is computed from the recorded columns by the visible table; a malformed row is refused with each problem named and none is dropped silently; a candidate with only vendor-side evidence ranks below every candidate with independent evidence.
parameters: evidence: Iterable[Evidence], today: Optional[datetime.date]=None, p: Params=DEFAULTS
inputs: Evidence rows, one per reported number, read from a CSV (esoi/evidence.csv by default) with the columns evidence_id, candidate, dimension, measure, value, unit, better, comparator, source_url, source_kind, run_by_independent, method_disclosed, n, benchmark_status, date_published, date_checked, confounds and note.
outputs: Dict[Tuple[str, str], Estimate]
effects: None: grading is computed in memory and no model is called. A malformed file raises EvidenceError naming every problem by line and column.
usage_notes: esoi evidence list, grade and rank read the records; evidence.estimates(rows) grades them from code. A conflict with the repository's own results is information, and the own result still decides the selection. See docs/how-to/use-public-evidence.md.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Specify from the Code
description: Spares people retyping what the code already declares, while leaving to them the text only a person can write.
purpose: Keep the records of a solution and its alternatives in step with the code that declares them, and create a new solution in one command.
approach: Read the declarations in the code and write only the missing rows with what the code knows, leaving a person's text untouched.
out_of_scope: Writing the intent itself, and importing the code it reads.
milestones: 1. Declaration sync: every declared solution or alternative missing from the records is reported, a second sync writes nothing, and a person's text survives. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: Decorator registries and plugin systems; schema derivation from code; the author's earlier pipeline decorators, which declare a stage once.
measures_of_success: A declared solution or alternative that the records lack is reported, the rows written are complete in what the code knows and empty in what only a person knows, and a second sync writes nothing. Standing conditions: What the code declares is in the records without retyping; the missing rows are written with only what the code knows; a new solution is one command; no cell a person wrote is overwritten.
parameters: The intent folder to write into; the id of a new solution.
inputs: The source files of the measured code and the intent records.
outputs: Findings (rule S30), the rows written, and for a new solution the records, a code skeleton and an evaluation folder.
effects: Writes record rows and, for a new solution, a module and an evaluation folder; never overwrites a cell that has text.
usage_notes: Run `esoi records sync` after declaring an alternative and `esoi new solution <id>` to start one, then write the text only you can.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Template Sync
description: Makes the author's own template wording the only definition of a record's fields, so the registry cannot drift from it or grow fields of its own.
purpose: Derive the registry's fields from the intent template in the skill so the author's wording stays the single definition.
approach: Read the fields from the template itself and report each field a record leaves unfilled after the template changes.
out_of_scope: Interpreting or extending the template.
milestones: 1. Template agreement: the registry's fields equal the template's fields and no required field is left empty after a refinement, and all template cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: The skill's `SKILL.md` as the source of truth; derived-copy practice already used for the standing instructions.
measures_of_success: A template refinement shows up as named missing fields on the next check, with no hand edit of any schema. Standing conditions: The registry's fields equal the template's fields after every refinement.
parameters: Path to the skill.
inputs: The skill's intent template.
outputs: A committed field list per type.
effects: Fails the check when the committed field list is stale.
usage_notes: Run after Joshua edits the template; public CI, which cannot read the skill, checks records against the committed list.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: ESOI Behaviour Judge
description: Grades the replies a pattern match cannot grade and shows how far its grading agrees with people, so a lenient judge is caught.
purpose: Grade whether one reply acts by the principles when a pattern match cannot tell, and show how far the grading agrees with people.
approach: Grade each reply against a rubric and score the grader against labelled replies, counting false passes and false fails apart.
out_of_scope: Grading general quality, and being the behaviour measure itself.
milestones: 1. Judge agreement: a person's label on a sample of recorded replies, and the judge's agreement with those labels recorded.
knowledge: Practice for model judges (agreement with human labels, preference for its own phrasing, position and length bias); the author's verdicts as the authority on what counts as acting by the principles; the case rubric of expected behaviour and failure mode.
measures_of_success: Agreement with human verdicts on held-out replies, with the two kinds of error visible, and a judge that passes everything is caught. Standing conditions: Every judge is scored by its agreement with labelled replies, with false passes and false fails counted apart; the labels move from the case author's to a person's; the judge is measured again when the model behind it changes.
parameters: The judge model, the rubric and the labelled replies.
inputs: A behaviour case and one reply.
outputs: A verdict (pass or fail) and a one-line reason.
effects: A model call per reply, which costs money.
usage_notes: Kept apart from ESOI Applied to AI Behaviour because its best is agreement with a person's verdict, not acting by the principles (docs/explanation/esoi-for-ai.md). Fill human_verdict in the judge's cases.csv to move the labels from the case author's to a person's; a behaviour score graded by a judge no person has checked is reported as such.
verdict_detail: the selected implementation has no recorded row; no arm has a result

name: Skill Distribution
description: Lets an author keep a skill in a private place and publish a complete, clean public copy that cannot go stale or leak.
purpose: Publish an author's skill from the private folder where it is maintained as a complete public folder that people install without anything else.
approach: Generate the public copy from the source, check it against the source, and scan it for private terms, paths and addresses.
out_of_scope: Deciding what the skill says, and hosting the published copy.
milestones: 1. Skill copy agreement: each public copy equals what the source generates and every planted leak is caught, and all skill cases pass. [met: 2026-10-26]
knowledge: The skill's own layout (one authoritative file and supporting notes); plugin and skill folder conventions of the agents that read them; derived-copy practice used for the intent template.
measures_of_success: After any edit of the source, a check names exactly what is stale; a planted private term, path or email is always caught; a fresh install equals the published copy. Standing conditions: The public copy always equals what the source generates, nothing private is in it, and installing it is one step in each of three ways.
parameters: The source folder, the include list, the substitutions, the list of private terms.
inputs: The author's skill folder and a list of private terms that is never published.
outputs: A public skill folder, a plugin manifest and marketplace file, and an installed copy.
effects: Writes the public folders; fails the check on a stale copy or a leak; an install writes into a skills folder.
usage_notes: Run the sync after the source changes and commit the result; run the check in a place that can see the source and the private terms; people install with the plugin, a download or the command.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: The ESOI Steps
description: Gives a person or an agent a stated order for applying ESOI, so the work neither stalls on what comes next nor skips the steps that matter.
purpose: Give the order in which to define and apply ESOI to anything new or changed, and say where to loop back when something changes.
approach: State the steps in order from why to what to how, mark the human steps, and name where to return when something changes.
out_of_scope: Restating what each record type asks, prescribing tools, and shipping the steps with the skill.
milestones: 1. Steps followed: one recorded trial by a newcomer and one by an agent following the steps on real work.
knowledge: The 2020 Project Documentation board checklist; the author's skill (definitions, intent template, principles); trials of people and agents applying the steps.
measures_of_success: Trials complete the steps without asking what comes next, with no silent skips, and end with a passing check and a checked metric. Standing conditions: Every principle is carried out by at least one step; human steps are marked; metrics and their checks come before implementations; the process names how it is itself improved.
parameters: The size of the work (a sentence per step for a small change, full records for a project) and the next milestone that sets how much structure pays for itself.
inputs: An intent stated by a person.
outputs: Linked records, a checked metric, measured implementations and a recorded selection; a short summary of how the steps were applied.
effects: None beyond the records written.
usage_notes: Read skill/evolvable-structure/steps.md; the one-hour guide is a short first pass through it. Edit steps.md in the author's skill and run `esoi skill sync`, never the copy here. Record a trial whenever someone follows the steps, and change the steps when a trial shows a confusing, skipped or missing step.
